summary: Training volume over the last 4 weeks has been very low — only 3 sessions recorded (one short open-water swim, one indoor ride, and one harder open-water swim on 30 August), which is well below what the plan prescribes. Sleep quality is consistently poor, with most nights under 6 hours and body battery readings frequently in the low-to-mid range, suggesting chronic under-recovery. With the Half Oceanman swim (5,000m) just 33 days away, the priority must shift immediately to rebuilding swim-specific volume and aerobic base while protecting recovery.
suggestions: With the Half Oceanman 5,000m swim 33 days away, your swim volume is the most urgent gap — commit to both pool sessions each week (Tuesday and Friday) and target at least 2,000m per session, building toward 3,000m by mid-September to give yourself confidence at race pace of 2:30/100m.

Your average sleep is well under 7 hours on most nights and body battery is regularly below 40 — prioritise 7–8 hours of sleep as non-negotiable, as no training adaptation can outpace chronic sleep debt at this stage of your build.

The open-water swim on 30 August produced a training load of 189 and average HR of 161 — treat this week's Tuesday swim as technique-focused rather than hard effort, easing back into pool rhythm before ramping intensity in Weeks 12–13.

The Treviso 10K is 41 days away (one week after the Half Oceanman) — the tempo run sessions in Weeks 11 and 12 (5:35–5:50/km) align well with your 5:45/km race target, so hit these consistently and they double as race-specific prep.

Given the very low recent training load, avoid jumping straight into the full 240-minute long ride on Saturday 5 September — treat Week 11 as a re-entry week, keeping efforts controlled at the lower end of prescribed power zones.
